activities.title: Why Constraints Matter
activities.activity_preamble: Economists frequently make decisions under limits such as budgets, resources, or policy restrictions. This activity introduces the need for constrained optimisation before any formal method is applied.
activities.intellectual_coherence_bridge: This first activity connects familiar economic optimisation problems to the central enquiry of how best outcomes can be found when feasible choices are restricted.
activities.learner_task: Study the explanatory material on constrained optimisation and complete a comparison workspace that distinguishes unconstrained and constrained optimisation. Record the role of an objective function, a constraint, and the feasible set in each context.
activities.expected_output: A completed comparison table that accurately explains the purpose of constrained optimisation and correctly identifies how constraints alter the optimisation problem.
activities.reasoning_orientation: Focus on identifying the function served by each concept rather than memorising terminology.
activities.self_explanation_prompt: How does the presence of a constraint change the choices available to a decision-maker?

required_materials.purpose: Explain the relationship between optimisation objectives, constraints, and feasible choices.
required_materials.specification: Concise teaching text introducing objective functions, constraints, feasible sets, and the motivation for constrained optimisation in economics.

key_relationships: optimal solution must satisfy the constraint

required_materials.purpose: Provide a learner-completed workspace for comparing constrained and unconstrained optimisation.
required_materials.specification: Editable comparison table with rows for objective function, constraints, feasible choices, and optimal solution. Learners complete all comparison cells; no completed comparison rows beyond column headings.

required_materials.purpose: Support review of the completed comparison table.
required_materials.specification: Diagnostic checklist covering conceptual accuracy, distinction between constrained and unconstrained cases, correct use of terminology, and explanation of feasible choices.

evidence_decision.reason: The activity focuses on conceptual understanding rather than interpretation from supplied evidence.

activities.title: Build a Lagrangian
activities.activity_preamble: Having established why constraints matter, learners now convert an optimisation problem into a Lagrangian representation.
activities.intellectual_coherence_bridge: The conceptual distinction between objective functions and constraints now becomes operational as both elements are combined into a single Lagrangian expression.
activities.learner_task: Study a worked example showing how a Lagrangian is constructed. Then use a different optimisation problem to create a Lagrangian function and record each component used.
activities.expected_output: A correctly constructed Lagrangian that identifies the objective function, constraint expression, and multiplier term using the supplied practice problem.
activities.reasoning_orientation: Focus on how the objective and constraint are integrated rather than on solving the problem.
activities.self_explanation_prompt: Why is the multiplier term needed when transforming a constrained optimisation problem?

required_materials.purpose: Model the process of constructing a Lagrangian from a simple constrained optimisation problem.
required_materials.specification: Worked example demonstrating identification of objective function and constraint before constructing a Lagrangian. Must use a distinct optimisation problem from the independent practice operand and must not reveal or complete the learner attempt.

required_materials.purpose: Provide an optimisation problem for independent construction of a Lagrangian.
required_materials.specification: Near-transfer practice problem containing an objective function and a single equality constraint. Distinct numerical and symbolic values from the worked example. No solution steps included.

required_materials.purpose: Provide a structured response surface for recording the constructed Lagrangian.
required_materials.specification: Learner-completed template with fields for objective function, constraint, multiplier term, and final Lagrangian expression. All entries completed by the learner.

required_materials.purpose: Support review of the independently constructed Lagrangian.
required_materials.specification: Diagnostic checklist covering correct identification of components, correct incorporation of the constraint, appropriate use of the multiplier, and accuracy of the final expression.

evidence_decision.reason: The supplied problem functions as a procedural practice operand rather than evidence for interpretation or judgement.

activities.title: Solve the System
activities.activity_preamble: Constructing a Lagrangian is only the first step; learners now use first-order conditions to obtain an optimal solution.
activities.intellectual_coherence_bridge: The Lagrangian constructed previously now becomes the starting point for a systematic optimisation procedure using first-order conditions.
activities.learner_task: Review the modelled solution process and then solve a different constrained optimisation problem by deriving first-order conditions and calculating the optimal values.
activities.expected_output: A complete solution showing correctly derived first-order conditions, accurate algebraic working, and valid optimal values satisfying the constraint.
activities.reasoning_orientation: Treat each derivative and equation as part of a linked solution process rather than isolated calculations.
activities.self_explanation_prompt: How does the first-order condition involving the multiplier ensure the solution remains feasible?

required_materials.purpose: Demonstrate the procedure for deriving and solving first-order conditions.
required_materials.specification: Worked solution using a distinct constrained optimisation problem. Demonstrate the procedure but do not disclose any values, equations, or solutions from the learner attempt operand.

required_materials.purpose: Provide a complete optimisation problem for independent solution.
required_materials.specification: Single constrained optimisation problem requiring derivation of first-order conditions and calculation of optimal values. Distinct from the worked example and unsolved.

required_materials.purpose: Provide a structured response space for recording derivations and solutions.
required_materials.specification: Learner-completed solution template with sections for first-order conditions, algebraic manipulation, solution values, and constraint verification.

required_materials.purpose: Support review of the completed optimisation solution.
required_materials.specification: Diagnostic checklist covering derivative accuracy, correct first-order conditions, valid equation solving, and consistency with the stated constraint.

evidence_decision.reason: The activity requires procedural problem solving rather than interpretation from evidence-based particulars.

activities.title: Interpret Shadow Prices
activities.activity_preamble: The final activity shifts from calculation to economic interpretation.
activities.intellectual_coherence_bridge: Having solved constrained optimisation problems, learners now connect the calculated multiplier to its economic meaning and significance.
activities.learner_task: Examine economic scenarios that include multiplier values and resource constraints. Analyse what the multiplier indicates about relaxing the constraint and record interpretations for each case.
activities.expected_output: Reasoned interpretations that correctly explain the economic meaning of the multiplier and relate changes in the constraint to changes in the objective outcome.
activities.reasoning_orientation: Focus on the relationship between the constraint and the value generated by an additional unit of the scarce resource.
activities.self_explanation_prompt: Why can the multiplier be interpreted as the value of relaxing a constraint?

required_materials.purpose: Provide inspectable economic cases containing constraints and multiplier values for interpretation.
required_materials.specification: Three short economic scenarios with stated optimisation context, constraint description, and multiplier value. Do not state the interpretation or conclusion.

evidence_requirement.purpose: Provide the particulars required to infer the economic meaning of multiplier values.
evidence_requirement.learner_action: Inspect multiplier values and scenario details, then justify the economic interpretation.

required_materials.purpose: Provide a learner-completed workspace for analysing and interpreting multiplier values.
required_materials.specification: Editable analysis table with rows for each scenario and columns for observed multiplier, interpretation, and implication of relaxing the constraint. Learners complete all analytical entries.

required_materials.purpose: Support review of the completed interpretations.
required_materials.specification: Diagnostic checklist covering use of scenario evidence, accuracy of interpretation, connection between multiplier and constraint relaxation, and economic relevance of conclusions.

evidence_decision.reason: Learners must inspect supplied scenario particulars before interpreting the meaning of multiplier values.
